chapter: Inside the Basie rhythm section and band family
title: Great bands as families: the Lunceford band
summary: They compare Basie with Jimmie Lunceford's band, which Greene first saw at the Lafayette with Curtis Simmons.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: It is a little bit of a funny thing that -- if you look at that band, the one we're talking of -- it's almost as though that was a type of person.
Now if you take the Luteford band -- there's like a type of person in that band. I mean, you know, you'd think they'd all been at the same school or had the same family, or something.
That -- you've put your finger on it. This is exactly it.
The really great bands were great families -- with their own character.

That's it. That's exactly it. That's the impression. That's the impression when you look at Jimmy Luteford's band. I saw them at the Lafayette Theater and I -- the first time I ever seen them, and Curtis Simmons and I were together. We walked in there and looked up on that bandstand, and looked how everybody was so neatly dressed and everything was clockwork, and they did their thing, and it was a beautiful thing to see, you know.
That's the way it was back in those days, you know.

They -- bands like that like to keep it that way. And, Basie came along and he did the -- he had his thing going. I felt that when I came in the band, how, you know, after I got in there and found what was going on, and the different personalities, and it was still -- you know -- it was still Basie's band, in other words.
And, we kept it going, you know. We had to keep it that way.
